architecture.title: Four separate systems
architecture.description: The physical world, the inner learning network, the outer observation models and the Neural app differ in role and in how they are started.
architecture.note: This is the structure as read from the source. The placement of these cards does not imply active calls or training-data connections. Outer currently has shared_latent=false, and PosteriorNet is not connected to the Neural app or to the automatic training coordinator.

nodes.title: Outer observation models

nodes.title: Shared service
nodes.description: service.step_once takes dt, temperature and seed. With a [core] section it calls engine.core_step; without one it falls back to the replay-only integrate.step.

nodes.title: Core.step
nodes.description: One physical step on the GPU: checks the contact census of the start, refreshes the held split, runs the solve, then the between-solve updates.

nodes.title: Projected Newton + CG
nodes.description: ProjectedNewton.step: Newton iterations with conjugate-gradient linear solves, preconditioned by the chain-band solve along each filament chain.

nodes.title: Terms inside the solve
nodes.description: SDF contact with a barrier, the face-area K_A law from node triples, and the thermal draw (Brownian kick) enter the same world-wide energy.

nodes.title: Fast modes
nodes.description: Fast degrees of freedom are sampled from their own probability law once every several steps (directive 14).

nodes.title: Kinetics between solves
nodes.description: Motor and bond binding and unbinding, growth and attachment, from the rate tables at the solved positions.

nodes.title: State laws
nodes.description: Between-step laws such as rest-length relaxation, applied at the solved positions after the kinetics.

nodes.title: Step record
nodes.description: The Newton record plus kinetics, state laws, thermal and timing entries; the service then advances its clock and records by policy.

architecture.title: PosteriorNet internal layers
architecture.description: Structure that separates training preparation, the encoder forward pass, the training loss and inference sampling.
architecture.note: M = number of methods, C = channels per method, Q = number of context entries, D = number of axes, H = hidden (default 32), K = mixture components (default 4). Scaler fit happens once during training preparation; inference reuses the checkpoint scalers. After encoder → ordered fusion → mixture head, the path splits into training NLL and inference draws. The covariance lives in logit space. It is a standalone API/CLI and is not yet connected to the Neural app or the automatic physics training loop. Support is the range given as input.

nodes.title: Training prep: scaler fit
nodes.description: Fits the mean and standard deviation of time, channel and context on training observations only. These statistics are stored in metadata and are not refitted at prediction time.

nodes.title: Inference input: saved scalers
nodes.description: The Predictor passes the scalers from the checkpoint metadata into the batch. The saved transform is applied to observations entering the encoder below.

nodes.title: Per-method input B×T×(1+4C)
nodes.description: time + value + observation mask + known SD + SD-present flag. Context is 2Q-dimensional: value and present flag.

nodes.title: Per-method GRU
nodes.description: One GRU(1+4C,H) per method. A packed sequence leaves out the padding.

nodes.title: Method embedding
nodes.description: Adds the method's learned embedding to the GRU's last hidden state (H dimensions).

nodes.title: Ordered concatenation
nodes.description: Lays out the observed method hiddens in contract order: MH + method presence M + context 2Q. Pooled mean/max is a separate optional branch.

nodes.title: Fusion MLP
nodes.description: Linear(MH+M+2Q,H)→SiLU→Linear(H,H)→SiLU.

nodes.title: Mixture head
nodes.description: Linear(H,K×[1+D+D(D+1)/2]). Produces each component's logit, location and Cholesky entries.

nodes.title: Logit-space covariance
nodes.description: Splits the head into logits, loc and Cholesky lower. The diagonal is softplus+1e-4; this is not a covariance directly in the original physical units.

nodes.title: Training branch: logit NLL
nodes.description: Ground-truth θ → u inside the declared support → logit(u). Trains on the negative of the mixture log density produced by the head. This path needs no sampling.

nodes.title: Inference branch: distribution samples
nodes.description: Selects a mixture component and draws correlated normal samples in logit space. Sigmoid and the inverse support transform turn them into parameter samples.

architecture.title: PosteriorNet training and inference
architecture.description: Follows the paths for labels, loss, checkpoint and inference, separately from observation encoding.
architecture.note: Train takes simulation or mathematical fixtures with explicit parameter labels. Outer observations are not latent answers. A fixture-trained model refuses inference on real observations, and what it returns carries calibrated=false and physical_validation=false.

nodes.title: CLI entry
nodes.description: train takes contract/data/output and predict takes checkpoint/records/output, then each calls the API.

nodes.title: Training and split check
nodes.description: Split check → model and train scalers → batches → Adam.

nodes.title: Logit-space NLL
nodes.description: Normalizes θ to u inside the support → logit(u) → full-covariance Gaussian mixture log density. Labels outside the support are rejected.

nodes.title: Optimization
nodes.description: Backpropagates logit_nll over the train batch and updates with Adam.

nodes.title: Save and reload check
nodes.description: Saves weights, metadata, diagnostics and hashes, and compares samples after reloading. Not a physical validation.

nodes.title: Inference result
nodes.description: Observation records → batch → joint samples and covariance. Also returns the unverified status of calibration, physical validation and OOD.

architecture.description: What the integrated engine now holds: declared properties, parameter layers, the stop rule, opt-in arms and new transport and membrane rows. Solid boxes run by default on the integration line; dashed boxes are plans or opt-in arms.

nodes.title: Engine Declaration
nodes.description: Needed so contact, area, permeation and fluid walls never depend on what a part is called.

nodes.title: Two parameter layers
nodes.description: Needed so no biological constant hides inside engine code and no engine constant is tuned per cell.

nodes.title: Osmotic law arms
nodes.description: Needed because the osmotic pressure of a crowded solution is not one fixed number, so the law is declared, not assumed.

nodes.title: Relative stop rule
nodes.description: Needed because an absolute stop labelled a step converged after zero iterations when its driving force was already small, so its physics was never computed.

nodes.title: Solver assist arms
nodes.description: Needed to cut the cost of each step without changing what the step must satisfy.

nodes.title: Networks, unified
nodes.description: Needed so the small networks around the engine can later merge into one large model.

nodes.title: Conforming fluid grid
nodes.description: Needed so fluid fills only the space nodes can occupy, with no grid inside rigid or excluded space.

nodes.title: Ions, pumps, channels
nodes.description: Needed so volume change comes from named solutes and not from one flow law.

nodes.title: Membrane reservoir
nodes.description: Needed because a real membrane releases area from several forms at different tensions, not at one.

nodes.title: Emergent cortex arms
nodes.description: Needed so cortex thickness is measured from the built network and not put in as an input.

nodes.title: Language hypergraph
nodes.description: Needed so every declared thing, unit and conservation law is one checkable graph.

Head-owned MultiTask adapter: shared representation → vector coefficients.

Caller supplies one token set/representation per node and reconstructs with

models.doc: Two-layer tanh MLP with explicit width, seed, and initialization scale.

models.name: SolverHeads
models.doc:
Named global heads plus masked node heads; no runtime binding.

Inputs: ``tokens=(type,key,value,token_mask)`` as in ``batch_tokens``;
``scalar`` and ``scalar_mask`` [B,N,F] (unit 1); ``basis`` [B,N,C,3]
(µm); ``basis_mask`` [B,N,C]; ``node_mask`` [B,N]. The scalar values at
missing positions may be nonfinite: they are excluded before arithmetic.

Edge-enabled inputs add ``edge_features`` and ``edge_feature_mask``
[B,E,F_edge], ``edge_mask`` [B,E], and directed ``edge_ids`` [B,E,2].
Caller-declared ordering must equal the checkpoint config; output row i
corresponds to input edge_ids[i]. Permuting all edge arrays together
permutes the edge output. Duplicate active IDs are rejected.

Outputs: warm [B,N,3] µm; node preconditioner features [B,N,1] unit 1;
capacity [B,1] estimated primitive count; optional edge preconditioner
features [B,E,1] unit 1. Masked nodes/edges are zero. No output represents
an accepted physical label. ``forward`` is the offline fitting/fixture
path, including random untrained outputs. Checkpoint consumers must call
``predict_head``, which requires a per-head training declaration; legacy
checkpoints load with ``legacy_unverified`` status until retrained or
explicitly re-established from source evidence.

views.summary: Shows the live energy-core step: the projected Newton solve with contact, face-area and thermal terms, then fast modes, kinetics and state laws.

views.summary: Reads time-ordered measurement records together and computes the many internal states that could explain those observations.

views.summary: Restores the hidden parts of a force record from its measured parts. Shows, one after another, the layers that read patterns in nearby time.

views.summary: Compares independent models that handle literature, force records and images. No single neural network combining all the outer models has been implemented.

views.summary: Looks inside the calculations of two image classification models, one at a time. Being in the same view does not mean the two models are chained together.

aleph/physics/integrate.py:2148.title: Advance the virtual world once
aleph/physics/integrate.py:2148.input: Takes the current positions, velocities and relations in the world, plus this step's time interval.
aleph/physics/integrate.py:2148.action: Computes relation changes, forces, fluid and motion, following the configured order and branches.

One calculation that moves simulation time forward by a fixed interval.
A substance that can flow. Here it is the surrounding medium that exchanges forces with objects.

aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.title: Estimate possibilities from observations
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.input: Takes time-series observations for each method, whether each value was measured, and the known experiment conditions.

aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.output: Produces numbers that show which combinations are more likely, where the candidates cluster and how widely they spread.
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.why: Used to represent the many parameter combinations that could fit the same observations.

aleph/cell/params.py:1.title: Engine layer and cell layer

aleph/physics/energy/osmotic.py:1.title: Osmotic law as parallel arms

aleph/physics/energy/osmotic.py:1.action: Three declared arms run on the same world and the same record format.
aleph/physics/energy/osmotic.py:1.output: Water flux across each surface under the chosen arm.
aleph/physics/energy/osmotic.py:1.limit: The three-arm commit (952fc22b4) is on branch codex/osmotic-models-1007 and is not merged here. A composition-dependent coefficient and a Donnan start arm are still in progress. Nothing here was run on a device.

aleph/physics/energy/newton.py:191.title: A step must reduce its own force
aleph/physics/energy/newton.py:191.why: Needed because an absolute stop labelled a step converged after zero iterations when its driving force was already small, so its physics was never computed.
aleph/physics/energy/newton.py:191.input: The step's own starting force F0 and the declared force tolerance.
aleph/physics/energy/newton.py:191.action: The Newton solve now stops at min(tol_F, 0.1 F0). It never stops earlier than the old rule.
aleph/physics/energy/newton.py:191.output: A step that has either moved or been recorded with the rule that stopped it.
aleph/physics/energy/newton.py:191.limit: Device record GPU-1007-BOOK16: W1 chain N=100 chain-mode oracle error / amplitude 0.110 before, 7.9e-7 after. The change is a solver default; the signed stage-1 contract and scorer are unchanged (the contract text is a draft for the PI). One chain size is one case, not a general result.

aleph/physics/energy/assist.py:1.title: Opt-in arms that speed up the same solve
aleph/physics/energy/assist.py:1.why: Needed to cut the cost of each step without changing what the step must satisfy.
aleph/physics/energy/assist.py:1.input: Carried velocities, a learned warm field, a learned preconditioner term, a contact list reserve, continuation, a Parareal skeleton.
aleph/physics/energy/assist.py:1.action: Each arm proposes a starting point or a correction. The final step still iterates to the force tolerance.
aleph/physics/energy/assist.py:1.output: Faster convergence to the same tolerance, recorded per step.
aleph/physics/energy/assist.py:1.limit: All arms are off by default and are written code. None has been measured on a device. A prediction not checked at full resolution must be labelled a surrogate.

aleph/learn/__init__.py:1.input: Records, SWEPT-row vocabulary, admission rules and the registry.
aleph/learn/__init__.py:1.action: Shared schema, admission, registry and backbone. Inner A inference, B learned coarse and warm start, C fluctuation, D instrument; outer models unified by modality.
aleph/learn/__init__.py:1.output: Registered models with their lineage and a posterior over the engine.
aleph/learn/__init__.py:1.limit: Framework and arms are written. No trained weight from this work is presented here, and the older networks are not recalibrated by it.

The equations for fluid flow in which inertia has little effect.
